prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: After the first round I have moved from B026 to B057. The decisive point is a physical one that I can apply as I would to my own field: Buchwald and Hartwig identified why amination failed with simple catalysts, namely slow C-N reductive elimination from palladium amido complexes and competing beta-hydride elimination, and they solved it by ligand design, bulky and electron-rich phosphines in one line and chelating or hindered ligands in the other. The mechanism is understood in elementary steps, which is the standard I ask for. The method is three decades old, independently reproduced everywhere, and routine in process chemistry. Attribution is as clean as anything on the shortlist: two laureates who independently made the reaction general, leaving a free place that I do not think should be filled. Of the candidates in play it is the only one where maturity, mechanism and credit are all settled enough to write a citation without qualification.
statement.case_against: The two reservations from round 1 remain and I do not think they disappear. First, the 2010 prize honoured palladium cross-coupling, so a reader may see this as a second award for the same metal and the same catalytic cycle. My answer is that the hard step here is different in kind, the C-N reductive elimination and the amido complex chemistry, but this is an argument for distinctness, not a proof. Second, Kosugi and Migita reported tin-amide coupling in 1983, so the priority record is not spotless. The citation word 'general' and the 'development of' wording carry real weight in handling this. Finally, my own preferred line of work, B026, is now unsupported and I should not pretend that its absence from other rankings is anything but information.

responses.point: Johan argues that C-N coupling is a simple, general, enabling method with industrial-scale consequences, that Buchwald and Hartwig give a clean pair, and that the Kosugi/Migita priority should be acknowledged in the citation without adding a third laureate.
responses.response: I now agree with the configuration and with the reasoning on credit. In round 1 I asked whether the expert record shows a new reaction or a development of an existing one. The tin-amide coupling of 1983 needed stoichiometric toxic tin reagents and was limited to a narrow set of substrates; what was new was a catalytic system, with the amine used directly and a base, whose scope came from ligand control. That is a different capability and it supports a two-name citation. I would write 'development of general' in the citation to carry that distinction, and I do not support a third name. On your concern about conceptual narrowness, I accept that it is a method for one bond type, but the mechanistic content, the reductive elimination problem, is exactly what makes it a reaction-design result and not only a useful tool.

responses.point: Xiaodong argues that C-N coupling is chemically distinct from the 2010 prize, because the bond type and the ligand problem of reductive elimination from amido complexes differ, and that the two-person attribution is clean while Kosugi's work is a genuine precursor.
responses.response: This is the argument the committee asked for in the chair's questions, and I find it convincing on its physical content. The 2010 work concerned carbon-carbon bond formation where transmetalation and oxidative addition set the difficulty; here the difficulty is the C-N bond-forming step from a palladium amido species and the competing beta-hydride pathway, and the ligand solved that. I would put this into the record as the separation from 2010. I disagree only mildly with your suggestion that Kosugi might justify a third name. A three-name prize would credit a precursor that did not give a general method, and it would blur the citation. I would acknowledge his work in the committee's background document and not in the laureate list.

responses.point: Heiner proposes a two-part prize pairing B057 with base editing credited to Liu alone, because the two are different in kind and show the breadth of chemistry.
responses.response: I accept B057 as the first part, and I understand the wish to show breadth. I cannot support B058 as the second part this year. The first reports are about ten years old, off-target deamination and long-term safety data are still accruing, and the 2020 prize for programmable DNA cleavage is a close predecessor. A Liu-only citation also leaves Komor and Gaudelli, who carried out the key experiments, and the independent Nishida and Kondo cytidine deaminase work, unresolved. You identify this cost yourself. I would also say that a second part is not needed for balance. A single well-founded achievement is a better prize than a pair in which one part is contested.

responses.point: Daniel argues that targeted protein degradation is a new design principle and modality, and that the maturity of the cross-coupling method does not by itself outweigh a new principle.
responses.response: I take the point that degraders are more novel as a design principle, and I agree that the reproduction and the solved ternary structures make the mechanism chemically defined. My difficulty is the one you and Chabes both raise: the PROTAC strand and the cereblon glue strand are two partly distinct discoveries, and three names cannot honour both. With no approved degrader, a prize now would honour a concept and its promise. I would not rank novelty above a complete, attributable achievement, because the credit has to be written in three names. I keep B004 as an alternative because I think it is likely to be ready once the attribution is clearer.

uncertainties: Whether the expert record supports the statement that the Kosugi and Migita tin-amide work could not deliver a general catalytic amination, which my citation wording assumes
Whether colleagues who read C-N coupling as an extension of the 2010 prize will accept the argument that the reductive elimination problem separates the two
Whether B004 attribution between the PROTAC and cereblon strands can be resolved in a later year, since I have kept it only as an alternative
I am working from memory of the detailed mechanistic and priority literature, and have not verified usage figures
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with a shortlisted candidate. I disclose that my research field of respiratory-chain electron and proton transfer is scientifically close to B026, which I have now dropped as my preferred part, and that I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose work is not on this shortlist. I have no institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi.
